title: A dictionary of scene light — twenty-four lights to find by time, place and feeling
intro: Lighting is easier to pull out on set when you remember it by the scene it serves rather than by its name. The entries are sorted into four drawers: the face, time and weather, night and interiors, and genre and emotion. Each drawing shows the layout from above or from the side, with one line on how to build it and one line on where to use it.
groups: Night and interiors — light with a visible source
caps: The same face looks wider, slimmer or strange depending only on where the key sits.
The sun and the sky are the biggest lamps there are. Choosing the hour is choosing the light.
At night, light looks natural only when its source can be seen in the frame.
Add colour and movement, and light starts to announce the genre.
items: Broad light
Key on the wide cheek turned toward the camera
The face looks wider and brighter — thin faces, an open impression
Short light
Key on the narrow cheek turned away from the camera
Slimmer and more sculpted — the default for interviews and drama
Clamshell
Soft light above the lens plus a reflector under the chin
Shadowless skin — beauty and cosmetics close-ups
Top light
One lamp straight overhead, no fill
The eyes sink into shadow — loneliness, interrogation, pressure
Under light
Light from below chest height, aimed up
A familiar face turns strange — horror, torch scenes
Kicker
From behind on the side opposite the key, grazing the edge of the cheek
A wider edge than a rim — action, strong characters
Golden hour
Just after sunrise or before sunset: sun behind the subject, reflector to fill the face
Warm memory — family and holiday ads, first meetings
Blue hour
20–30 minutes after sunset: the sky is the key, interior lamps add warm points
Stillness and loneliness — the cut into the city at night
Overcast
The whole sky is a giant softbox; a black flag on one side restores shape
Stable skin tones — documentary, interviews, outdoor product shots
Midday sun
Hard light from overhead — move into shade or rig diffusion above
Heat and dryness — summer, desert, the city at noon
Window light
The window is the key; leave the room side dark or lift it with a white card
Everyday life and reflection — the cheapest and most luxurious light
Dappled leaves
Branches or a cut-out board (cucoloris) in front of direct sun
A fresh afternoon, memory, summer
Moonlight
High back light with blue gel (CTB); keep the face low-key
The basis of night scenes — real moonlight is too dark to record
Day for night
Shoot backlit by day, underexpose two stops, grade blue, keep the sky out of frame
Wide night landscapes you cannot light
Street lamp
Hard orange or white light from high up, shadows falling to the feet
The walk home, isolation, the city at night
Candle and firelight
Flame in frame plus a small warm lamp low and out of frame, flickered
Intimacy, confession, ritual
Screen glow
A small cool panel where the monitor or phone is, at low output
Late nights, isolation, messaging scenes
Venetian blinds
Pass hard light through blinds or window bars
Noir, entrapment, secrets
Volumetric light
Haze in the air and hard light from behind — the beams become visible
Mystery, reverence, music videos
Neon and mixed colour
Two sources of different colours left and right — magenta and cyan are typical
The city at night, clubs, a cyber mood
Warm key, cool rim
Key warm (around 3200 K), back light cool (5600 K or more)
The subject separates from the background — most advertising
Spotlight
One narrow beam on the subject, everything else black
Stage, confession, a hero's declaration
Flashes
Strobe or lightning effect in short repeated bursts
Tension, shock, clubs and action
Passing light
Lamps moving outside the frame — car headlights, train windows
The passage of time, inside a moving car
note_t: A source, not a name — motivated light
note: First decide which source in the frame could produce the light (a window, a lamp, a screen, a street lamp), then make the real lamp imitate its direction and colour. Audiences read light with a visible source as natural and light without one as lighting.
lens: A world that bends into a circle — skating, music videos, POV
Tilt the barrel to move the sharp spot
A hole instead of a lens
Endless depth, but a soft picture
filt: 4, 6 or 8 rays depending on the grooves
Darkens only the top of the frame
Bright sky and dark ground together
Align the transition with the horizon so it does not show
Doubled images and rainbow fringes at the edges
Turn it by hand in front of the lens to create movement
